headline: Meta emphasizes connection, impact, and AI innovation; DEI language peaked 2020–2021, then receded sharply by 2026.
identity: Meta has consistently valued social impact, openness, and technical excellence across its careers messaging, with a strong emphasis on building products that connect billions of people. Altruism and inclusion language surged from 2015–2022 (peaking around 2020–2021 with explicit DEI framing), but both have wavered significantly by 2025–2026, where AI and hardware innovation dominate the narrative at the expense of human-centered values. The company's commitment to diversity and belonging, once central to its employer brand, has been substantially deprioritized.
fit: You might be a good fit if you are energized by fast-paced, high-impact technical work on products used by billions, comfortable with risk-taking and rapid iteration, and drawn to cutting-edge AI and hardware challenges. However, if inclusive culture and explicit commitment to diversity are important to you, note that Meta's recent messaging has shifted away from those themes—the careers copy now leads with technological capability and innovation rather than belonging or community values.

sections.heading: The Rise and Fall of DEI Language (2013–2026)
sections.body: Meta's careers copy embraced explicit diversity and inclusion messaging starting around 2013 ('be yourself,' 'authentic selves'), with intensity building through 2015–2018. The peak came in 2020–2021, when DEI language appeared in 12–16 chunks per year with explicit demographic targeting ('students from underrepresented communities,' 'Veterans,' 'women,' 'faith groups'). By 2022, DEI remained present but began to soften; by 2023–2024, it had contracted to thin data (2 chunks). Most strikingly, in 2025–2026, DEI language nearly vanishes from the mission-brand sections—inclusion scores drop from 0.59 (2020) to 0.16 (2026), and the register shifts from 'explicit_demographic' and 'belonging_culture' to 'absent.' The company's stated commitment to 'building a team that reflects the diversity of the people' has been replaced by technical product descriptions.
sections.body_2: This is not a gradual fade but a sharp reversal. The 2025 copy still mentions 'inclusion strengthens our workplace' and 'diverse backgrounds,' but these appear in process/logistics sections rather than mission statements. By 2026, all 11 mission-brand chunks focus exclusively on AI products, Ray-Ban glasses, and Llama models—no mention of diversity, belonging, or community values.

sections.heading: AI Becomes the Dominant Narrative (2019–2026)
sections.body: AI language was nearly absent until 2019 (4.8% prevalence), then spiked dramatically: 8.3% in 2022, 44.4% in 2025, and 100% in 2026 (all 11 mission-brand chunks mention AI). The 2025–2026 copy emphasizes 'Llama,' 'Meta AI,' 'multimodal reasoning,' 'Ray-Ban Meta glasses,' and 'AR wearables'—technical capabilities rather than human values. Quotes shift from 'we're determined to build a better, more connected world for everyone' (2015–2018) to 'Muse Spark powers Meta AI with natively multimodal reasoning' and 'Meta Llama significantly elevates code generation, reasoning and content translation' (2026). The company's self-description has transformed from a mission-driven connector of people to a hardware and AI innovator.
sections.body_2: Notably, the 2025 copy does mention 'build the future of AI openly and responsibly' and 'human connection,' but these are framed as technical outcomes, not values. By 2026, 'human connection' disappears entirely from the visible messaging.

sections.heading: Altruism and Craft Remain Stable; Performance Messaging Declines
sections.body: Altruism scores stayed relatively consistent from 2009–2019 (mean ~0.15–0.27), spiked in 2015–2018 (0.25–0.28), then dipped in 2019–2024 before recovering slightly in 2025 (0.22). Craft language (quality, excellence, building great things) remained modest throughout (mean ~0.06–0.10), with a small uptick in 2022–2023. However, performance language—'move fast,' 'tackle big stuff,' 'immediate impact'—was strongest in 2009–2015 (0.55–0.56 mean), declined sharply by 2019–2021 (0.43), and has remained low through 2026 (0.25). This suggests Meta's careers messaging has de-emphasized urgency and speed in favor of technical depth and innovation.
sections.body_2: The shift is subtle but consistent: early Meta (2009–2015) recruited for 'people who like to move fast and tackle the big stuff'; recent Meta (2025–2026) recruits for 'people who want to build the future of AI.' The former emphasizes hustle and impact; the latter emphasizes capability and vision.
